title: The condensed reduction O_E → O_E/ℓ^{n+1} is a map of ring objects
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], topologized by its absolute value [def-sfb-coefficient-extension-integers-topology], and $n\ge0$. Give $\mathcal O_E/\ell^{n+1}\mathcal O_E$ the discrete topology. The morphism of condensed abelian groups $\underline{\mathcal O_E}\to\underline{\mathcal O_E/\ell^{n+1}}$ between the continuous-function condensed rings [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], given on each profinite set by composing continuous maps with the reduction $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_E/\ell^{n+1}$, is a morphism of ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]: it is compatible with the units and the multiplications.

source.place: sk-def-sp-tate-twist: sk-def-sp-tate-twist (Lean Sheaf.Paper.ProEtaleTateTwistsOfUniverses, which imports Sheaf.Paper.ProEtaleTateTwists): the reduction O_{E,X} → (B_{E,n+1})_X of the integral Tate twist is coefficientMap of spEllPointReduction, a ring map by this instance; Lean: SHEAF file lean/Sheaf/Paper/ProEtaleTateTwists.lean, declaration AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.spEllPointReduction_isMonHom (module Sheaf.Paper.ProEtaleTateTwists, lines 155-162, proof `sorry`)

proof.text: Put $O=\mathcal O_E$, $I=\ell^{n+1}O$ and $B=O/I$ with the discrete topology. The quotient map $q:O\to B$ is a unital ring homomorphism: $q(a+b)=q(a)+q(b)$, $q(ab)=q(a)q(b)$ and $q(1)=1$ by the quotient operations. By [lem-sp-ell-quotient-finite-discrete], $q$ is continuous for exactly the absolute-value topology on $O$ and the discrete topology on $B$ in the statement. Thus postcomposition with $q$ sends a continuous function $S\to O$ to a continuous function $S\to B$.

source.place: Integral-twist formula with finite coefficients O_E/ell^n; continuity supplied by the cited quotient lemma, as in spEllPointReduction in lean/Sheaf/Paper/ProEtaleTateTwists.lean:145-153.

proof.text: For each profinite $S$, set $F_S(a)=q\circ a$. By [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] the section rings have pointwise operations. At every $s\in S$, $F_S(ab)(s)=q(a(s)b(s))=q(a(s))q(b(s))=(F_S(a)F_S(b))(s)$ and $F_S(1)(s)=q(1)=1$; similarly $F_S(a+b)=F_S(a)+F_S(b)$ and $F_S(0)=0$. Hence $F_S$ is a unital ring homomorphism. For $u:S'\to S$, $F_{S'}(a\circ u)=q\circ a\circ u=F_S(a)\circ u$. These are precisely the restriction maps in the cited node, so the $F_S$ form a natural transformation of the underlying ring presheaves. Since both are already sheaves by that node, this is a morphism of sheaves of rings.

source.place: First three sentences: continuity, sectionwise ring laws, and commutation with precomposition, specialized to the quotient map q.

proof.text: Apply part 3 of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] to the sheaf-of-rings morphism $F$ of step 2 on the coherent site of profinite sets. It states that a morphism of sheaves of rings is a morphism of their underlying ring objects, for the sheafified objectwise tensor product over $\mathbf Z$. The underlying abelian-sheaf map has exactly the components $a\mapsto q\circ a$ specified in the item, so it is the given reduction map $f$. Consequently $f\circ\eta_O=\eta_B$ and $f\circ\mu_O=\mu_B\circ(f\otimes f)$. These are both required compatibility equations, for the canonical ring-object structures, and prove the claim.

source.place: Final paragraph: a morphism of sheaves of rings gives a morphism for the canonical counit-transported ring objects.
